subject: general
question: A train passes two bridges of lengths 600 m and 200 m in 80 s and 40 s respectively. The length of the train is:
solution:
**Given:**

Length of two bridges be 600 m and 200 m respectively 

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculation:**

 Let the length of the bridge be LB₁,length of the 2nd bridge be LB₂

 Length of the train be LT 

 Here, train passes through bridge having length of 600 m in 80s

 Whenever, train passes through bridge, then length of the bridge is added to the length of the train

⇒ LB₁ + LT = Speed of the train × 80 

⇒ 600 + LT = S× 80 ( Where, S = Speed of the train)

 LT = 80S - 600 ......................(1)

 Now, LB₂ = 200m , time = 40s

⇒ LB₂ + LT = S × 40............. .( Put the value of Length of the train from equation (1) 

⇒ (200 + 80S - 600 ) = 40S

⇒ 40S = 400 

⇒ S = 10 m/s.

Now, Length of the train =( 80S - 600) =( 80 × 10 - 600 ) = ( 800 - 600 ) = 200m

**Hence, Length of the train is 200m.**
